title: Early intravenous then oral metoprolol in 45,852 patients with acute myocardial infarction: randomised placebo-controlled trial
authors: Chen ZM, Pan HC, Chen YP, Peto R, Collins R, Jiang LX, et al.; COMMIT (ClOpidogrel and Metoprolol in Myocardial Infarction Trial) collaborative group
followUp: scheduled treatment until discharge or up to 4 weeks in hospital; mean 15 days in survivors
population: Patients admitted to 1250 hospitals in China within 24 hours of suspected acute myocardial infarction; 93% with ST-segment elevation or bundle branch block and 7% with ST-segment depression
funder: The funding statement of the trial report could not be read: the publisher page requires a subscription. Registry NCT00222573 names the University of Oxford as lead sponsor and Sanofi and AstraZeneca as collaborators. Industry collaboration sets the class to industry.
result: Metoprolol up to 15 mg intravenously then 200 mg orally daily (n = 22,929) against placebo (n = 22,923). Neither co-primary outcome was reduced: death, reinfarction or cardiac arrest 2166 (9.4%) against 2261 (9.9%), odds ratio 0.96 (95% CI 0.90 to 1.01); death 1774 (7.7%) against 1797 (7.8%), odds ratio 0.99 (0.92 to 1.05). Per 1000 treated, metoprolol prevented five reinfarctions (464, 2.0%, against 568, 2.5%; odds ratio 0.82, 0.72 to 0.92) and five episodes of ventricular fibrillation (581, 2.5%, against 698, 3.0%; 0.83, 0.75 to 0.93) and caused 11 more cases of cardiogenic shock (1141, 5.0%, against 885, 3.9%; 1.30, 1.19 to 1.41). The excess of shock arose mainly on days 0 to 1, when the overall effect on death, reinfarction, arrest or shock was adverse; net hazard was substantial in haemodynamically unstable patients and net benefit moderate in relatively stable patients after days 0 to 1.
